summary: Monday hooks-and-retention pass, built around the owner's 31 Oct notes (animation 5/10, hooks lack curiosity, cinematic music dull). Added 6 topics (4 core, 1 local India) and 3 experiment proposals: a 'you think X? wrong' hook, money that travels between props instead of popping in, and a cinematic music bed with a pulse.
why: Our 'secret' hooks (claims) get 11.0x median views and 156% kept past the hook against 1.05x for 'question' hooks (n=4 vs 8). The McDonald's contact sheet shows wide, static shots with money as small tags from 5 to 45 s. Cinematic is our best genre (13.4x, n=6), but the owner called it a 'postmortem'. The feed had 8 open topics and no local one.

findings.title: The owner's suggested hook matches our numbers
findings.detail: Claim hooks ('secret') keep 156% past the hook and 75% viewed; question hooks that half-answer ('It's not the burgers. So how...') get 38%. Proposal hook-you-think-x-youre-wrong.

findings.title: The animation problem is visible in the stills
findings.detail: v-20261031-01: every build beat from 5 to 45 s is a wide shot with money as small tags; nothing moves between the props even though the story is money moving. Proposal money-travels-not-pops.

findings.title: Rich vs Poor Mindset is the fastest Short in the niche
findings.detail: 2.2M views in 4 days (60 s). Added a rich-vs-poor $50K car topic with an 8.8M reference.

findings.title: 'Starbucks is a bank' has proven demand
findings.detail: PolyMatter 1.2M, ColdFusion 650K, WSJ ~900K. Added as a how_they_make_money topic with illustrative maths.

findings.title: Claude Code 2.1.314 and 2.1.316
findings.detail: Subagent effort level setting; cloud scheduled tasks are now marked failed when auto mode stops a turn. Nothing for the pipeline to change.
